title: stabilize-sse-chunking-and-delimiter-handling-to-preserve-json-objects-and-token-order
author: Aisha Banerjee
commits: Normalize CRLF handling and explicit chunk boundary parsing
Add buffer-resume logic to reconstruct JSON tokens across chunk boundaries
Add integration tests for multi-event-per-chunk and token-split cases
Fix delimiter trimming logic that dropped leading whitespace for structured outputs
Docs: inventory streaming edge cases and recommended client parsing behaviour
release_notes: Fixes intermittent corrupted JSON payloads and mis-ordered function/tool-call events in SSE streams caused by chunk boundary tokenization differences and delimiter trimming. Improves streaming reliability for structured output and OpenAI-compat clients. No breaking API changes.
description: Motivation: Multiple customers and internal e2e tests revealed flaky behavior in the OpenAI-compat SSE stream where partial JSON objects or function-call payloads arriving split across TCP/SSE chunks could be parsed incorrectly by the SDK and server-side consumers. Fail modes included truncated JSON in the last event of a chunk, swapped ordering between token events and "event:" markers when a chunk split mid-token, and delimiter logic that inadvertently consumed leading whitespace for structured outputs. This PR consolidates fixes across the compatibility shim and the runtime streaming sink to make SSE framing deterministic and robust. Changes: 1) Introduce a canonical chunk parser in packages/redwood-openai-compat that preserves raw chunk boundaries but builds a resilient buffer to reconstruct JSON tokens when events span multiple chunks. The parser now handles CRLF and LF uniformly and treats a bare "data: [partial]" line as append-to-buffer rather than emit. 2) Add explicit event-buffer-flush semantics in the runtime stream sink (stream-sink.cpp) so that tokenization and "event:" ordering are preserved even under Nagle/segmentation behaviour. 3) Harden delimiter trimming: only strip a single trailing CR/LF sequence from the end of a completed event, do not trim leading spaces that are semantically significant for structured outputs. 4) Add comprehensive integration tests (sse-framing.test.ts, python sse test) that simulate multi-event-per-chunk, CRLF-in-chunk, and token-split-across-chunks scenarios, plus a small stress harness used in CI to reproduce the race observed in production. 5) Update docs/api/sse.md with recommended client parsing patterns and a troubleshooting checklist. Testing and CI: Local and CI runs replicate the previous flaky scenarios; initial CI runs surfaced a transient timeout on the python test which was a test harness race; I adjusted the harness to use deterministic flushing and all checks now pass. ci_status is passing. Review discussion: Marco flagged the original implementation for over-eager trimming and requested defensive tests for function/tool-call event ordering; Samantha requested a clearer comment block around buffer ownership in stream-sink.cpp which I added; Jonah suggested adding a small debug flag to emit chunk boundaries in dev builds which I implemented behind an opt-in build macro. Rollout and compatibility: This is fully backward compatible at the API layer; clients that relied on earlier trimming quirks will only notice improved fidelity. Rolling to canary with a small percentage is recommended to ensure no downstream clients assumed the previous faulty behavior. Merge: Squash-merged after approvals and green CI. Notes: I validated against examples/structured-output to ensure function call payloads are emitted intact and against the SDKs (TS and Python).
